examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: Compare the ranks of A and the augmented matrix [A|b]. Unequal ranks mean inconsistency; equal ranks give solutions, unique only when the common rank equals the number of unknowns. For homogeneous equations consistency is automatic, and free-variable count is columns−rank. A zero determinant alone does not distinguish infinitely many solutions from none for a nonhomogeneous system.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
A system has 6 unknowns, rank(A)=rank([A|b])=4. How many free variables are present?

**Answer: 2.** Equal ranks make the system consistent. Four pivot variables are determined in terms of the six minus four free variables. Thus there are 2 free variables and infinitely many real solutions.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
When introducing a parameter, check every value that makes a pivot or determinant zero separately; elimination steps that divide by that expression exclude those cases.

Having as many equations as unknowns does not guarantee a unique solution.
